## 2026-11-17: how the machines reach each other: liveness, the home's key and its addresses, and Devices says how (research/97 steps 1–3)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D293 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, core, runner, CLI and workers, web, Mac, iPhone, Android): research/97's first three steps. Checked by tests with fake clocks, fake sockets and fake homes, and in shots against a demo core (`.shots/d293/`); not yet on a real tailnet, a real Cloudflare account, a real second network or a Mac that really sleeps.** *Who:* the heavy developer most (a server in a tailnet, a MacBook doing tasks for it, a phone that is sometimes in the tailnet and sometimes not); the consumer with a Mac at home and a Cloudflare tunnel; the fresh user never sees a network word. *Feel:* before, a laptop that changed Wi-Fi left a dead socket for up to two minutes and then lost its running sessions; a home had one address, chosen by whichever command ran last, and switching meant pairing every device again; nobody could see which way a device was connected or that a tunnel lets Cloudflare read the traffic. After, a blip is a calm "reconnecting" and the same session carries on, a home keeps every way to reach it, every native device picks the best way that proves it is the home, and Devices says plainly how each device is connected. *First time:* nothing new to do: the next welcome carries the ways, and the card shows them. **(1) Liveness.** Every socket on the home is pinged (a WebSocket ping every client answers by itself) every 15 s and cut after 45 s of silence (`core/src/workers.ts` `createLiveness`, one sweep for client and worker sockets). A worker pings every 15 s and redials after 45 s without an answer, and at once when its ping timer fires more than 10 s late (the computer slept) (`cli/src/uplink.ts` `createPinger`). A client pings only a home whose welcome says `ping: true` (the web every 15 s, also skipping one interval when the browser paused the page; the Mac app with a 45 s read deadline), so a 0.0.60 home is never closed for silence. The Mac app says `{t:"sleep"}` on its own socket at system sleep and dials nothing until it wakes, then at once (`client.Sleep`, `Wake`, mygo's power events); the home marks the worker on that Mac's computer asleep too, so its tasks read 睡着了 / Asleep at once (the worker process can't hear the system's sleep itself). **(2) A worker's sessions survive a drop.** The worker keeps one host for the life of its process; after a drop it holds its sessions for 2 min and keeps what they say (at most 5000 frames, else the grace ends early); its hello after the drop names the sessions it still holds (`held`); the home holds them 2 min 15 s, ends the ones not named and reattaches the rest, and the buffered frames flush in order after the welcome. A worker from before D293 names none, so its sessions end as before. In the task: the residency is offline and work in flight says **正在重新连上 {device}… / Reconnecting to {device}…**; back in time: **{device} 连回来了，接着做 / {device} is back; carrying on**, the same session, nothing resumed; past the grace the old path (resume by id), and the wait before **在等 · {device} 连不上** counts from the drop, not from the end of the grace. Never failed, never blocked during the grace. **(3) The home's key.** Ed25519, made at first start in `<dataDir>/home-key.pem` (0600, beside `devices.db`), never printed; the fingerprint (SHA-256 of the raw key, first 16 bytes, base64url, 22 characters) rides in pairing links (`/pair#c=<code>&k=<fp>`: the code is still read by every older parser), in the pairing answer (`fp`, `key`, `ways`), the welcome (`fp`) and the ways frame. `GET /.well-known/ducter-home?n=<nonce>` answers before the gate (a device asks a way before it shows that way its token) with the key and its signature of `ducter-home\n<nonce>`; a device accepts a way only when the key's fingerprint is the one it pinned (the link's `k`, else the pairing answer, else, for a device paired before D293, the first welcome over the token it already had). **(4) The address book.** `<dataDir>/reach.json` (0600, no secrets): ways `{kind: lan | tailnet | domain | tunnel, url}`. `ducter domain`, `ducter tailscale` and the Cloudflare tunnel each add or take out their own way and never overwrite another; `public-url` stays as the primary, the address pairing links lead with and the only one an older client knows: the first way added is the primary, a later one leaves it alone, and when the primary goes the next that reaches the most devices takes it (domain, tunnel, tailnet). A `public-url` from before D293 is a way too and joins the book when another is added. The tunnel no longer refuses to start beside a domain in the book; only an address set by hand (`DUCTER_PUBLIC_URL`) still counts as "own". The running home reads the book every 5 s (the CLI writes it from another process), checks each way from itself every 5 min by the same challenge, and calls a way up whenever a device is connected through it now (a machine often can't open its own ts.net name). The list goes to every client and worker after each welcome and whenever it changes (`{t:"ways"}`); `lan` is reserved for step 4 and nothing adds it. **(5) Devices pick their way.** The rules are one module (`packages/protocol/src/reach.ts`, mirrored in Go, Swift and Kotlin): nearest first (same network, tailnet, domain, tunnel; then the primary), each tried 250 ms after the one before, the first that proves it is the home wins unless a better one still pending answers within 300 ms; while connected, a look every 30 s at the way in use and every better one: leave a way only after two misses in a row (for the best one that answered), move up only after a better one answered twice in a row. Workers do it on every redial and every 30 s, keeping their sessions through the switch (the grace); the CLI picks once per command for a home in `home.json`; the Mac app races at launch and runs the keeper every 30 s, retargeting its socket; the iPhone and Android apps race on coming to the front and when the page can't reach its home, and every 30 s only leave a way that stopped answering (a move reloads the page, so moving up waits for the front). The iPhone and Android apps keep the device record (token in the Keychain, or the app's own storage on Android; device id and name) so a page opened at another origin asks the app for it (`{t:"device"}`) and is the same device. Android verifies Ed25519 from Android 13; before it the app stays on its one address. The web page stays on its own origin (storage, push and the service worker are bound to it) and lists the other addresses. Switching ways never needs pairing again. **(6) Devices says how.** A connected worker's and a client's card: the header **怎么连着 / How it's connected**, one row: **经由你的 Tailscale 网络 / Through your tailnet** · **经由你的域名 / Through your domain** · **经由你的 Cloudflare 通道 / Through your Cloudflare tunnel** · **同一个网络 / Same network** · **就在这台电脑上 / On this same computer**, its muted line **全程加密，中间谁也看不到 / Encrypted all the way; nobody in between can read it**, through Cloudflare (a tunnel, or a domain behind Cloudflare's proxy) **加密到 Cloudflare 为止，Cloudflare 能看到内容 / Encrypted as far as Cloudflare, which can read it**, plain http on a network **没有加密，同一个网络里的人能看到 / Not encrypted; others on the network can read it**, on the home's own computer **不经过网络 / Never leaves this computer**. The home reads it off the request that opened the socket (its Host against the book; Tailscale serve's and Cloudflare's own headers), so it needs nothing from the device and works with every client version. The home's card: **能连到 {home} 的地址 / Addresses that reach {home}**, a row per way: the kind (**Tailscale 网络 / Tailscale network** · **你的域名 / Your domain** · **Cloudflare 通道 / Cloudflare tunnel** · **同一个网络 / Same network**) over its address, and at the right **连得上 / Reachable** · **连不上 / Can't reach** · **还没查过 / Not checked yet** · **在用 / In use** (the way this window uses); under it, with a tunnel, **经过 Cloudflare 通道的内容，Cloudflare 能看到。其他地址全程加密。/ Cloudflare can read what goes through its tunnel. The other addresses are encrypted all the way.**, and on the web **这个页面一直用打开它的地址……/ This page stays on the address it was opened at…**. ## 2026-11-17: earlier sessions in the person's own agents come along (research/100 item 4; motivation reason 1: the author's current agent workbench is winding down and his work has to "move to Ducter tomorrow"; research/103)

| D299 | **Built 2026-11-17 (core, runner, protocol, the web wide and phone, the Mac app), checked with synthetic sessions in the installed agents' own record shapes and fake runtimes; not yet against a real model or a real person's sessions.** *Who:* the heavy developer whose last month of Claude Code and Codex sessions (and pi's) sits in `~/.claude`, `~/.codex` and `~/.pi`, outside Ducter, and who wants to find "the Raft snapshot one" and carry on in Ducter, not start over; the consumer who used Claude Code by hand once and finds that afternoon in the same place; the fresh user who has no such sessions and never sees the section. *Feel:* before, moving to Ducter meant leaving every earlier conversation behind (D45 said start fresh); after, the first open of Past tasks already holds their own work, under **也在这台电脑上 / Also on this computer**, and one tap carries the very conversation on, with its earlier turns above. *First time:* nothing to turn on; the section is there in Past tasks when such sessions exist, with one quiet line saying what it is. **(1) Shown by default, read lazily and locally.** Read only when Past tasks asks, on the home, only each file's head and tail (sessions reach a GB, research/103 §4), kept until the file changes; never sent anywhere but the person's own clients; never read by a model to list. Ducter's own sessions are never listed (their ids are in the Log; its data folder, the Ducter folder and temporary folders are left out); a session carried on already is listed as its task. The ⋯ menu's **不再显示 {agent} 的 / Don't show {agent} here** hides one agent for good (`outside.json` on the home, every window told); the section's last line **不显示的：{agents} / Not shown: {agents}** with **再显示 / Show again** brings it back. Chosen over opt-in (a setting the heavy developer would turn on in the first minute anyway, and the consumer never finds) and over an import step (copies the person would then have two of). **(2) Found by D285's search.** The same field, time words and agent and project chips find a session by its name (the person's `/rename`, Claude Code's own title, pi's `--name`), the person's first and last words, its folder and project (a worktree another agent workbench made counts as its repo), its branch and its agent; every word must match; starred and tags narrow to Ducter's tasks only. **(3) The card** is D285's: the picture guessed from its words by the same rule as a task's, its name, the person's first words (or where the words matched), and one small line of project, agent, branch and day, each its own word (no " · " joins, D291); a folder no longer there says **文件夹不在了 / Folder gone** and can't be carried on. **(4) 接着做 / Continue** makes it a Ducter task working in the session's own folder directly (no copy: the person worked there by hand and their own git is the undo), whose transcript opens with **在 {agent} 里开始的，{day} / Began in {agent} on {day}**, the last 60 turns of the conversation (the person's words and the agent's; tool calls stay in the session, which the agent reads itself), then the hairline **{time} 在 Ducter 里接着做 / Picked up in Ducter at {time}**. The same agent resumes that very session by its id (Claude Code `--resume`, Codex `thread/resume`, pi by id in its folder, through OAR), told where it came from; it appends to its own file as it does by hand, and Ducter never writes that file. **换一个 agent 接着做 / Continue with another agent** starts the other agent in the same folder from what the session said (D282's condensed start: the person's last words to it and its last words); a resume the agent refuses falls back to the same. Again on the same session opens its task. The partner hears a quiet note; its Past card says **从 {agent} 接过来的 / Carried on from {agent}**. **(5) One reader for two features:** `packages/core/src/local-agents/` lists projects and sessions and summarizes one, for this and D298's first greeting. *Not taken:* forking the session (`--fork-session`) so the original file stays byte-for-byte (two copies of one conversation, and by hand the person would no longer find Ducter's turns); importing every session into the Log (gigabytes of tool output, privacy for nothing). *Open (todo):* a worker's sessions (an op over the worker link), Codex's own thread names from its database, New task from this for an outside session, a real-model run of a resume. ## 2026-11-17: a usage limit is a wait, not a failure (research/100 item 3, research/101; scenario A4; principle 13)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D297 | **Built 2026-11-17 (runner, protocol, core, partner context, web, Mac) and checked by tests with each agent's limit shape from source (research/101), fake clocks and fake runtimes, a home restart and the hand-off; not yet against a real limit hit on any account, on a worker, or by a person.** *Who:* the heavy developer whose overnight tasks stopped when Claude Code's 5-hour window ran out (before: a failed turn, a task that read 在做 until morning, nothing done); the consumer, who never hears the word limit unless it matters; the fresh user, who sees a ring and one sentence. *Feel:* before, a limit was a failure from nowhere; after, 放心: it says when it carries on and does, by itself, in the same session. *First time:* the first limit any task meets; nothing to set up. **(1) Detection, in the runner** (`limit-hit.ts`): a failed turn OAR classes `quota` (or `rate_limited`, a throttle that outlived the agent's own retries) is a limit, never an error line; its reset, best first: OAR's `resetsAt` (Claude Code's `rate_limit_event`), the used-up window the session said just before (Claude Code's event as read by D288, Codex's `account/rateLimits/updated`), the agent's own words (Codex "try again at 3:12 PM" / "Nov 18th, 2026 3:12 PM", Claude Code "resets 3am (Asia/Shanghai)" and "usage limit reached\|<unix s>"), else unknown. The runner logs one line (`raw.limit`), no nudge; the failed turn says nothing of its own. **(2) The default: wait and carry on** (`core/limits.ts`): the task rests on a wait of its own (D267's `wakes: "task"` timer with `limit`), at the reset plus a minute's grace, and then gets **{agent} 的额度恢复了，接着做刚才没做完的。** in the same native session (resumed by id, D282), a home restart included (the wait is in the Log; overdue, it carries on at once). No reset known: it tries again (10 minutes after a throttle, else hourly, at most a day, then the person's turn). **(3) One account, one reset:** a task whose agent named no time takes the reset another task on that account was given, and a newly named reset moves the rest; On hand draws two or more under one line, **Claude Code 的额度 3:12 恢复 / Claude Code's limit resets 3:12** with **这 3 件到时一起接着做 / These 3 carry on together then**, each task still its own card. **(4) The card** (D279's look: the clay ring filling toward the reset, the time left inside): **Claude Code 的额度用完了 / Claude Code's limit is used up**, **额度 3:12 恢复，到时接着做 / The limit resets at 3:12, and it carries on then** (unknown: **额度恢复后接着做，4:10 先去试一次 / It carries on once the limit is back, and tries again at 4:10**), then **现在换 Codex 接着做 / Hand it to Codex now** (only when another signed-in agent on the same computer can take it: not limited itself, not paid per use, D89) through D282's in-task switch, carrying the task's progress, and **先停下 / Stop here** (the wait ends, the task is the person's turn; 不等了 and Stop waiting not taken: D279's raters read "stop waiting" as deleted, and the result is that it stops). The state word everywhere is **额度 3:12 恢复 / Limit resets 3:12**, the row's line **等 Claude Code 的额度恢复 / Waiting until Claude Code's limit resets** (in the viewer's language, from the agent, not the logged reason), the transcript's hairlines **Claude Code 的额度用完了 / Claude Code's limit ran out** with **额度 3:12 恢复** apart, and **Claude Code 的额度恢复了，接着做 / Claude Code's limit came back, carrying on** with its time apart (D291); the end line **等 Claude Code 的额度恢复** with **额度 3:12 恢复** apart. **(5) Hand off automatically** is the person's choice, made where it matters: a quiet switch under the card's buttons, **以后额度用完，直接换别的 AI agent 接着做 / Next time a limit runs out, hand it to another AI agent right away** (`Settings.limitHandoff`, off by default; not a Settings pane, D296's panes are another change). On, a limit with someone to take it is handed over at once (no wait; the transcript says the limit ran out, then D282's **换成 Codex 接着做**). **(6) The partner only when it matters:** a limit wait never wakes it, except once when no reset is known and nobody else can take the task (`limit.tell`); it reads the waits and their end in its context, and is told to mention one that happened while the person was away with the task's result ("昨晚 Claude Code 额度用完，3:12 恢复后接着做完了"). *Defaults the author may revisit:* hand-off off by default (an automatic move to another agent changes who works on the person's code); a minute's grace after a reset; unknown resets tried hourly for a day; pay-per-use agents never offered (they cost money; D89 says so before anything costs). *Alternative not taken:* hand off by default (faster, but a silent change of agent at 3 am on someone's repo is the kind of surprise principle 14 forbids). *Not built (todo):* the partner's own limit (its harness hitting one); a worker's limit read from its own account; an eval scenario for the morning line; OAR upstream carrying Codex's reset. | research/100, research/101, A | `packages/runner/src/{limit-hit,normalize,runner}.ts`, `packages/runner/test/limits.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/{limits,waiters,work,core,ws,settings}.ts`, `packages/core/test/limits.test.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/{index,transcript}.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/{transcript-cases.ts,transcript.json}`, `packages/partner/src/{render,partner}.ts`, `apps/web/src/{i18n-limits,i18n,work,onhand,transcript,app}.ts(x)`, `apps/web/static/app.css`, `apps/web/{demo,demo-limits}.ts`, `apps/web/test/limits.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/{i18n/limits.go,i18n/limits_test.go,protocol/protocol.go,views/{limits,limitcard_test,work,onhandlist,onhandboard,taskpage,taskturns,transcript}.go}`, `design/{product-model,focus-window,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/waiting-and-routines.md`, `research/101-limits.md` |

No model runs (nothing may be signed in yet, and the first second costs nothing). The words are per-language tables picked by the hello's language (D292; a language without a table gets English). (Folder: {~/path})** and never sends; then one everyday example (three when there are no records). It is in the Log, so the partner knows it said it (its context shows what was offered); said once (a second app sees the same message). Mem's line about the person is a hook (`FirstWordsInput.memLine`), left for D295. D204 rejected guessing where code lives (a list of folders under `~/dev`, `~/code` … that the person must correct). The records Claude Code and Codex keep are not a guess: they are the exact folders the person chose to work in, written by tools the person runs, about work the person did; Ducter exists to carry that work on. Read only, through D299's reader of those records (`packages/core/src/local-agents/`, shared with Past tasks; `recentFolders` in `first-words.ts` picks from it): file names and times, and from each of the newest 40 files of the last 14 days per agent its folder, title and first words (head and tail, bounded); never inside the folders themselves; Ducter's own sessions (its data folder, its Ducter folder) and temporary folders left out; never sent anywhere except as the first words, which go where the person's own words go, to the model they chose. **On by default, with a one-tap no in place**: under the starts, **从这台电脑上你的 {agents} 留下的记录里看到的：只在这里读，只给你看。/ Found in what your {agents} keep on this computer: read here, shown only to you.** and **别再看了 / Stop looking** (`local_agents` frame, `settings.json` `localAgents: false`): the starts from the records go at once, the line becomes **好，以后不再看这些记录。/ Fine, I won't look at those records again.** with **还是看吧 / Look again**; with it off the first words never read them. Alternatives: ask before looking (a question before the first hello is a form, and for most people the answer is yes; the visible no right under what was read keeps the person in control); never look (the partner's first words stay generic, research/100 item 1). (3) **The clay partner over its first words**, while nothing else was said: the empty screen's character, waving once (still under reduced motion), then the bubble, then the starts two to a row (one on a phone). No "new" line over it. (4) **Paste a key, no subscription needed.** Recognised by shape (`packages/protocol/src/api-keys.ts`, research/102 §1): Anthropic, a Claude Code sign-in token, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi (China and international), Alibaba Model Studio, Zhipu GLM and Z.ai, Google Gemini, xAI, Groq; a plain `sk-` key is a list of candidates, settled by the check. **Checked with one call that spends nothing** (`packages/core/src/api-key.ts`, research/102 §2): the account's balance (DeepSeek, Kimi, OpenRouter), the key's own record or the model list, at the address the agent will use; the first candidate that knows the key wins. In the conversation (Mac and web) whenever nothing on the home can think (`first_screen.noBrain`): under the first words, else above the composer; the `key_add` frame. Settings and Devices are D296's (a todo). ## 2026-11-17: 替你做过的 / Done for you, the record of what Ducter did on the person's behalf (research/100 item 8; scenario G5; principle 18; research/104)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D300 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, core, the partner's tool, the web wide and phone, the Mac app), checked with a seeded day and fakes, and the partner eval's two new scenarios on haiku; not yet against real accounts.** *Who:* the developer at the end of a day of eight tasks ("did anything merge, touch an account?"), the consumer who gave it mail, a card and a phone ("what did it send in my name, what did it pay?"), the fresh user who meets it as a quiet line and usually sees the empty day first. *Felt:* 放心 above all: everything it did in their name in one short list, each with the Go they gave. (1) **The place: 替你做过的 / Done for you** (zh title, link and the Mac menu 替你做过的… / Done for You…, ⌘⇧Y), a whole-window place on the Mac and a sheet on the web like Past tasks; not a Settings pane. Reached from On hand's end (beside 做过的事 ›), one quiet line under the morning note, the Mac's menu, and the partner. Rejected names: 它替你做过的 (the partner has its own name; "it" adds nothing), 对外记录 / Outside record (a system word), 账本 / Ledger (money only). (2) **What counts:** only what left the task's own place or used something of the person's: sent (mail and messages through an account, a send or post tapped in an app after its Go, a message to another agent over Bridge), paid (a saved card after Pay, a pay or buy tap), called (every call placed, with how it ended), sign-ins and fills (saved sign-ins and details, keys given), changed (calendar, merge, draft PR, a folder task's files, a setting or install in an app, any other account write), deleted, and looked at (each account per day and task, **counts only, never content**). Not in it: the partner's own replies, work inside a task's own place, anything held or failed before it went out. A send never confirmed says 没确认送到 / Not confirmed; a call no one answered 没人接 / No answer. (3) **One card per action:** a drawn glyph per kind on a clay pebble, the line from a table by kind (发邮件给 {to} / Mailed {to} …), the thing's own words under it (≤ 140 chars), then each fact its own element (D291): who asked (你让它做的 / You asked · 任务「…」 · 例行「…」), the Go (你点了好 {time} / You said Go at {time} · 没人回，按默认做了 · 之前允许过), where (在 {device} 上 · Ducter 的手机 · 用 {line} 的号码 · 用你自己的号码 · 通过 {account}); 打开任务 / Open the task, 看结果 / See it, and **改回去 / Undo only where one truly exists** (a folder task's copy, D142). (4) **Days like a diary**, newest first, each with its counts as separate facts; a field that searches as you type; filters by kind with counts; 更早的 / Earlier adds a week; the honest coverage line at the end (commands a task ran directly on its computer aren't here). **The empty day:** the clay character with its notebook, 今天没有替你发出、付过或打过什么。/ Nothing sent, paid or called for you today., and what did happen as facts. (5) **Nothing new is stored:** the record is derived at read time from the Log and Autofill's uses (`core/src/did.ts`); protocol `did` → `did_result` (`protocol/src/did.ts`). (6) **The partner answers from the same list:** a read-only tool `did_list` (when: today / yesterday / week; kind), actions kept apart from the counts of looks; one persona line ("asked what you did for them: did_list first, with the kind"). Eval `did-today-zh`, `did-today-en` (2/2 on haiku, run with `--only`; the full eval is rerun after the parallel merges, D175). | research/100 item 8, research/104, G5 (`flows/G-safety.md`), principle 18 | `did.md`, product-model glossary, scenarios G5, `docs/done-for-you.md`, todo |

Warm dark paper (`#17120E`, surfaces `#231C16`/`#2A221B`, brown-black, never grey); every card and button keeps its ledge (a near-black base, `#0D0A07`); the ink button turns cream with dark words on a taupe ledge; the quiet button keeps the paper with a faint light rim; each state's surface goes deep and its ink light, its dot keeping its hue; the tints are `MidnightTints`; the Devices sea goes to dusk (same scene, the light low and warm); the picture viewer and the title moment were already dark. Clay art is cut out and reads as it is; the Codex coin, whose charcoal knot would vanish, takes its D213 dark cast (`coin_codex_dark`, the web's, 128 px: the coins draw at 64 pt or less) through `theme.Clay`, which gives an asset's `_dark` cast while the window is dark. No view hard-codes a colour (a grep found only brand marks on app tiles, the sea's alpha shadows and the title's black, all theme-independent by design). **(2) The setting.** Settings › 外观和声音 / Look and sound › 外观 / Look gains **浅色和深色 / Light and dark**: **跟随系统 / Follow the system** (the default; the glossary's word, the same as the Language row under it, not a new "跟着系统 / Match the system"), **浅色 / Light**, **深色 / Dark**, under the Pebble row; D296's layout kept. Kept in the Mac's own `desktop.json` (this Mac only, like Language); it also sets MyGo's `Theme.SetSource`, so the menus, the title bar and the window's first paint (`light-dark(#FFF6EA, #17120E)`) agree. **(3) The change.** Live: MyGo re-renders on macOS's appearance change and the window reads it each frame. Every colour moves from one paper to the other at once over 360 ms on an ease in and out (`theme.Blend`, `AppearDur`), the way a room's light changes: no second copy of the page drawn over it; at once under Reduce Motion. **(4) Contrast (WCAG 2.x, `theme/contrast_test.go` fails below AA in dark; light / dark):** Ink on Bg 14.7 / 15.8, on Surface 15.7 / 14.3; InkSoft on Bg 9.8 / 11.7, on Surface 10.5 / 10.6; InkMuted on Bg 5.3 / 6.4, on Surface 5.6 / 5.8, on SurfaceSunken 4.6 / 6.1; Ink on Chrome 15.2 / 15.4; the user's bubble 6.7 / 6.7; the partner's bubble 15.7 / 13.3; on the accent 6.7 / 6.7; the ink button's words 14.7 / 15.8; highlight 6.3 / 7.6; added 7.5 / 9.1; deleted 8.5 / 9.1; a reply's quote on the partner 4.4 / 5.9, on the user's orange 3.5 / 5.4; the viewer's bar 17.2 / 18.7; state inks on their surfaces: needs you 6.4 / 9.3, working 7.8 / 9.8, waiting 6.7 / 10.8, done 6.6 / 10.1, failed 7.1 / 8.7, awake 6.6 / 10.1, asleep 7.8 / 9.2, away 6.2 / 8.8 (each on the paper 6.9–14.4); tint inks on their grounds 5.2–6.9 / 6.5–7.2; big numbers in Strong (3:1) 3.1–4.8 / 6.7–9.2. ## 2026-11-17: WeChat as a window on the one conversation, through WeChat's own ClawBot (research/100 item 7: "no chat window for Chinese users"; research/105; research/79 §2)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D301 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, core, the web wide and phone, the Mac app), checked against a fake iLink and a fake CDN only; never on a real WeChat account.** *Who:* the consumer in mainland China whose life is in WeChat and who can't reach Telegram; the heavy developer in China whose phone is WeChat; the fresh user, who knows "扫一扫" and nothing else. *Felt before:* the partner lives only in the Ducter app. *After:* 放心 first: nobody signs in as them and their WeChat account risks nothing; 好用: one scan, nothing to paste; 顺滑: the same conversation in the app they already open; honest about what WeChat allows. (1) **The route is WeChat's own ClawBot over iLink**, the one official way for a person's own agent to talk with them in WeChat: a QR scan binds a one-to-one ClawBot contact to the scanner, the home long-polls (no public address), no real-name step for one's own binding. Never unofficial protocols or hooks that log in as the person (their whole social life and WeChat Pay at stake); WeCom's long-connection bot, Official Accounts and self-built WeCom apps are not this (in WeCom, or a business and a public domain). (2) **Ducter's own client of the documented protocol** (`channels/wechat.ts`); Tencent's MIT package was read for the protocol, nothing of it is used or run. It says who it is: `bot_agent: Ducter/<version>`, `channel_version: 2.4.10-ducter` (the protocol's version first, as its document asks of other hosts). (3) **The scan is the pairing:** `confirmed` names the scanner (`ilink_user_id`), who becomes the one linked account; nobody else can add the ClawBot, and anyone else's words are still ignored (D276 (5)). No code to type; WeChat's own number is passed on when it asks; a QR that runs out is replaced three times, then Settings says the QR ran out and that their WeChat may not have ClawBot yet. Unlink is Disconnect. (4) **It answers, it doesn't push:** caps `replyWindowMs` (23 h) and `windowSends` (9), both a little under what is reported (about 24 h, about 10, secondhand). Anything, a turn's answer or what Ducter starts itself, goes to WeChat only inside that window; outside it the place falls back to the app and push carries it. WeChat refusing a send closes the window until the person writes. (5) **No buttons, no edits:** a reversible card ends with 回「好」就{go}，回「先等等」就先放着。/ Reply "ok" to {go}, or "wait" to hold it. (the hub's typed words); Open in Ducter carries the home's address written out when it has one; no Still on it line. (6) Pictures, files and video both ways through WeChat's AES-128-ECB CDN; voice comes in as WeChat's transcript. Replies carry the newest `context_token`; typing through `getconfig`/`sendtyping`. A stale token (-14) is Can't connect: 微信要你重新扫一次码。, never a retry loop. (7) **Settings › 聊天软件 gets a WeChat group** (between Slack and iMessage, the sage tint, 微 / W): off says 用微信自己的 ClawBot 连 with two steps; scan shows the QR (on a phone too, with the screenshot hint) and 不连了 / Cancel; linked says 和你的微信连着, whether it can reach them now, and the rule in one paragraph; its privacy line says it is WeChat's ClawBot and that Ducter never signs in to their WeChat. | research/105, research/79 §2, research/100 item 7, D276, D283 | `channels.md` §9, product-model glossary, scenarios H7, `docs/chat-apps.md`, todo |

## 2026-11-17: rich answers, a table, a chart, a list to tick or answers to tap in a reply (research/100 item 5: "answers are text only"; motivation.md "world-class generative UI")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D303 | **Built 2026-11-17 (protocol, the partner, the web wide and phone, the Mac app), checked with unit and fixture tests on both clients, the Mac test renderer, headless Chrome against a demo core, and the partner eval's five new `rich-*` scenarios on haiku with `--only` (the last two runs 5/5 and 4/5); the full eval is rerun at the merge (D175).** *Who:* the consumer who asks "compare these two" or "how did last week go" and got a paragraph of numbers; the developer asked "which repo?" who types its name; the fresh user, who must never meet markup. *Felt:* 好用 and 赏心悦目: a comparison or a week reads at a glance, a choice is one tap; 放心: the numbers are the real ones; nothing extra when a sentence will do. (1) **Four kinds, only when asked for:** a table (a comparison), a chart (bar or line, one series, numbers from a tool, a report or the person, never remembered or guessed), a checklist (a list to tick), choices (a question with 2–5 short answers; a tap sends that answer). Never for one fact, a yes/no, a greeting, a task's result, or anything needing Go: that stays a decision card (rule 7 now says "choices about the work"). Persona section "Rich answers" (about 1.5K characters; the budget ceiling raised to 24.2K). (2) **The format:** a fenced ```` ```ducter-ui ```` block of one JSON object (`type` table / chart / checklist / choices; the limits: 2–6 columns and 1–12 rows of cells up to 80 characters; 2–14 points with a required one-sentence `summary`; 1–12 items, `tell` to hear back; 2–5 distinct options up to 40 characters; 4000 characters a block, three a message, one choices). Rejected: tool calls (a block belongs in the words, where it stands; a tool adds a turn and a schema to every request), Markdown tables (no chart, no choice, unreadable in chat apps), HTML or a free component tree (a page, not a reply; unsafe; can't degrade). (3) **The home validates and degrades it** (`protocol/src/rich.ts` `parseRich`, in the partner's message path): a valid block is stored on the message (`ai_msg.ui`, with its `plain` text) and replaced in `text` by that plain text; a bad one is left out and counted (`uiDropped`), which the partner reads in its history; a message that would be empty keeps its JSON as code. So chat apps, pushes, Copy, memory and older clients all get one text that reads: a table one line per row, a chart its sentence and its points, a list or choices `- ` lines, with the reply language's punctuation (a `words()` table, D292). (4) **One drawing model on both clients:** a client splits the text at each block's plain text (`splitRich`; a block it can't find goes last, a kind it doesn't know stays as text) and draws from `richModel` / Go `ModelOf` (numeric columns; the chart's scale from zero to a round top in at most five steps of 1, 2 or 5; numbers with at most two decimals, grouped thousands; "%" and "°" hug, any other unit a space); `fixtures/rich.json` is passed by the web's model and the Go port. (5) **The look (Pebble, tokens only, light and dark):** the day card's white on its clay base; a table's head small and muted, row labels bold, numbers right-aligned in even figures, a wide one scrolling sideways in its card on a phone; bars in the accent clay with a lighter top and a ledge, a line in the accent with hollow points, a dashed line per step and the zero line solid, values over bars and points when eight or fewer; checklist boxes on a ledge, a ticked one in the done tint with its item struck through; choices as clay pills under the question. (6) **Behaviour:** a choice's tap sends its words as the person's own message (no pictures, no reply-to); choices work until the person says anything after the message, then stay as a record, theirs in the accent, the rest faded. Ticks stay on the device (web `localStorage`, the Mac's `desktop.json`); only `tell: true` adds **报一下进度 / Send progress**, which sends **勾好了：{done}。还没：{left}。/ Done: {done}. Not yet: {left}.** (or all / none) at any time. (7) **Accessibility:** a real table (headers by column and row; Mac table, row, header and cell roles); a chart is an image whose words are its sentence then each value (the web adds a hidden table); checklist items are checkboxes; choices a labelled group. | research/100 item 5, motivation.md, principles 7 and 20, D129, D222, D236, D254, D291, D292, D302 | `conversation.md` "Rich answers", product-model glossary, scenarios H8, roadmap, `docs/tables-and-charts.md`, todo |

Only when the recall changed the answer, at most one per reply, never a list of what it read, never the memory's text. Supersedes D295 (a)'s "in the reply's Details": inside Details nobody would see it, and the point is trust at the moment of the answer. **(2) The mechanism: a mark the code checks.** memory_search gives each result a short ref (`m1`, never Mem's id) and who saved it; its result note says: only if one of them changed what you say, end that message with its ref, `[[m1]]`. Code takes every mark out of the words before they are logged (no client, chat app or the Log ever sees one), resolves the first against this turn's results only (an invented or stale ref makes no line), and logs one `memory_recalled` (memoryId, title, by, from, date, aboutSeq) right after the message; a mark said alone goes under the words before it. Chosen over a new tool (a call per answer, ≈0.4K in every session's prefix, latency) and over a reply tool the partner doesn't have; the tool list and the persona are unchanged. **(3) Tapped:** 它想起的这条 / What it remembered: the title, who it is from and the date as separate facts (D291), **这次的回答用到了它。**, **忘掉 / Forget** asking in place (another tool's: **…，{tool} 那边也一样。**: forgetting is Mem's and reaches every tool; D295's read-only for other tools' memories now holds for Settings only), and **在 Nowledge Mem 里打开 / Open in Nowledge Mem** (Mem's site; no documented link to one memory yet, todo). A forgotten line disappears on every client (`MemView.forgotten`). **(4) 这周记下的 / What it learned this week.** The week's first morning note (Monday's, or the first after a Monday it missed) carries one line, **这周记下了 {n} 件关于你的事，要看看对不对吗？** with **看看**, when it noted anything in the last 7 days and memory is on; never in the notification; a quiet Monday still shows it (without a push). No Sunday-evening note: the morning note is the one place it speaks unasked (D250). The sheet: each line **对** (kept as checked), **改** (the person's words; `nmem m update --title --content` through the partner's Mem client; **改好了，Nowledge Mem 里那条也改了。** or, without an id or when Mem refuses, **这里改好了；Nowledge Mem 里那条没改成。**), **忘掉** (asks). **(5) Other tools' memories in task briefs.** At a task's start the existing recall (title + brief, 4 hits) now also runs where the person's Mem plugin is there; then only other AI tools' memories are named, ≤ 3, by id, tool and title, in `<from_your_other_tools>`, for the agent to read through its own plugin (the person's own memories come from the plugin; contents never travel). Where Ducter's recall stands in, `<what_i_know>` lines say **saved by {tool}**. **(6) Measured** (haiku, `--only`): the three new scenarios pass (recall used → one line by "said"; another tool's → one line by "tool"; a general question → none), and `mem-recall-last-time-zh`'s ack got its line unasked; `mem-recall-person-en` (length) and `mem-down-zh` fail as they did before this change on haiku. | U (the D304 brief), D295, D250, D168 | `memory.md` "In the conversation (D304)", product-model glossary, scenarios J12, `docs/settings.md`, todo; `packages/partner/src/{partner,memory}.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/mem-source.ts`, `packages/core/src/{settings,ws}.ts`, `packages/core/src/proactive/engine.ts`, `packages/runner/src/{brief,runner}.ts`, `apps/web/src/recall.tsx`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/recall.go` |

It goes away when it's done.**; a call that goes live while the app is open shows by itself, once (removed, it isn't put back). The Lock Screen card and the Dynamic Island: the same pebble mark (its dot when it needs you), the title, the phase in the glossary's words (在做 · 在等 · 等你 · 做完了 · 没成 · 已取消; 在打 · 通话中 · 对方在问 · 打完了 · 没人接 · 没打通), and how long, each its own element (D291); past the stale date **可能不是最新的 / May be out of date**. **Words-free over the wire:** a Live Activity push can't be sealed (no extension opens it, unlike D159), so the content state is `{phase, since}` only; the title is set on the phone and never leaves it. The home (`core/src/ambient.ts`) follows the Log and pushes only a change of phase (priority 10 for needs you and the end, else 5), with a 4-hour stale date; the end dismisses after 15 minutes and the follow is forgotten; a dead token or a disconnected phone is forgotten; at most four per phone. Out through this home's own Apple key, or the relay's new `activity` op with a separate handle kind for activity tokens, where **the relay builds the payload itself from a phase it validates**, so no home can put words on a Lock Screen. Behind `DUCTER_LIVE_ACTIVITIES` until a real iPhone checks the push path. **(3) Android: one ongoing, silent notification** per followed task or live call (channel **跟着看的任务和通话 / Tasks and calls you follow**, low importance, no sound or badge), offered as **在通知栏显示 / Show in notifications**; the title, the phase and a live clock; Android asks for notifications at that tap if it never asked. No push from the home yet, so the page keeps it true while the app lives, and it **times out after 20 minutes without a fresh word**, gone rather than wrong (a finished one rests 15 minutes). The loan's notification (D246, D255) is unchanged. *Alternatives not taken:* a count beside the Mac's mark (reads as debt, changes with every task); a Live Activity per running task (a stack that nags, and Apple limits them); sealing the content state with the phone's key (no hook to open it); the title in the content state (the Lock Screen is readable by anyone holding the phone, and Apple and the relay would see it). | research/100 item 9, research/107, D71, D159, D246, D287, D291 | product-model glossary, `ui.md`, scenarios K4 and K5, todo, `docs/on-hand.md`; `packages/protocol/src/ambient.ts`, `packages/core/src/{ambient,web,core}.ts`, `apps/site/api/push/[op].ts`, `apps/web/src/ambient.tsx`, `apps/desktop/{main.go,internal/views/tray.go,internal/theme/tray.go}`, `apps/ios/{LiveShared,DucterLive}`, `apps/ios/Ducter/GlanceLive.swift`, `apps/android/.../Glance.kt` |

## 2026-11-17: a routine run closes at its turn's end (research/108 B3: "routine tokens counted as 0 on Claude Code")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D308 | **Built 2026-11-17, checked with the fake clock and tests in the real order (report, then usage); not yet run live.** A routine run's *result* is set by its report (done or failed, the first one), but the run *closes* at its turn's end: its tokens are the usage that turn reports, or, if the residency leaves `hot` (or a turn end comes) without a usage line, what was seen so far. A reported run waits at most 2 minutes (`CLOSE_WAIT_MS`) for that, then closes with what it has; the next firing closes it first; a restart closes it on the way back with the usage already in the task's stream. Why: on Claude Code `report_to_main` is a call inside the turn, so the turn's usage comes after it; closing on the report recorded `tokens: 0`, so D114's per-run budget (2x the first run) was never set and the month's count stayed 0. The other option, counting usage after a closed run toward its month, was not taken: it loses the per-run record the per-run budget is built from. ## 2026-11-17: a session of 10,000–100,000 events opens, scrolls and jumps without holding it all (the author: "conductor-like ai 界面，那个 minimap 要考虑比如上万条消息的大 Session，怎么从下往上滑动的时候按需加载之类的，不能卡顿，浪费内存")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D320 | **Built 2026-11-17 on the web and the Mac (test renderer), checked by perf tests over a synthetic 2,000 / 10,000 / 50,000-event review loop and headless Chrome against the demo core (`DEMO_LONG=50000`); not yet on a real long loop or reviewed by the author.** *Who:* the developer with a loop running for days (before: the page grew with every page it loaded and never let go, a 10,000-event task took 0.6–0.9 s per older page on both clients, a 50,000-event one never reached its head, the locator knew only what was loaded); the consumer opening a long errand from the phone (memory and battery); the fresh user (nothing to learn: it scrolls like a chat). *Felt:* 顺滑 and 放心: the page moves at once both ways, the locator shows the whole session from the first moment, a click far away lands. *First time:* opening any long task. **(1) A session index from the home.** One small row per turn (`packages/protocol/src/session.ts`): its first and last seq and count, when it began and last moved, what opened it as its block with texts cut to 200 characters (the brief, the person's words, the partner's, a wake, Ducter's note, a Go relayed: the same `promptOf` that cuts turns in the transcript), about how tall it draws settled (16 px steps from what opened it, whether it holds steps, its last words' length), its compactions, switches, moves, retunes, interruptions, reports and the first plan; the session's count, newest seq, latest report and wakes. The home makes it once from the stream (pages of 5,000 by its (stream, seq) index) and then adds each event the Log appends (`core/src/session-index.ts`, the 64 tasks asked about last); `task_index` answers it, or its turns from `fromSeq` on after a new socket; each client adds live events with the same `indexAdd` (both ports pass `fixtures/transcript.json`'s `index`). 50,000 events: 2,084 turns, 351 KB (about 7 KB per 1,000 events, gzipped with D284's frames), made in 5 ms. **(2) A window both ways.** The page lays out every turn of the index; a client holds at most `WINDOW.keep` 1,500 events around what is on screen plus always the newest `WINDOW.tail` 200 (what the rest of the app reads), letting go when it holds 300 more (`keepFor`: two thirds of what it keeps lie ahead of the scroll); `nextAsk` asks one page of 300 at a time, the turns on screen first, then 600 events ahead of the scroll and 300 behind, growing the stretch next to them (`task_history` `beforeSeq`, or the new `afterSeq` for a far stretch growing down) or, with nothing near, starting 100 events before the turn. A task nobody has open keeps its newest 2,000. D284's background pages up to 2,000 are gone where the home sends an index (kept for a home before D320). The place is kept by the first turn on screen (the Mac's `ui.List` by key; the web by that turn's place in the content), so a page landing or leaving never moves what is read; a reader at the end stays at the end. **(3) Turns built one at a time.** `slotsOf` gives every turn of the index; a turn is built from its own held events, with what it needs from before it (`BuildCtx`: the brief said, the latest report, the event before, more after), only when it is drawn or read, and kept until its events change; a page or a live event builds only its own turns; a turn with nothing held is a blank of the index's height; a turn of more than 1,000 events is built from its newest. Built alone, every turn equals building everything at once (the fixtures), except that the app a run of browser steps is in no longer carries from the turn before. **(4) Drawn only near the screen.** The Mac's list already builds only rows in view; the web now draws the turns within a screen of the view and two spacers (`vlist.ts`), heights measured once drawn, else the index's. **(5) The locator from the index:** the whole session on the rail and in the list; a click on a turn not held goes there at once, its blank first, and tints when it lands; a near one keeps D284's glide. D279's count of wakes is the whole session's. **(6) Huge items:** a text over 20,000 characters (an output, a command or a note over 8,000) is cut before its keys are hidden and drawn; **显示全部（{n} 字）/ Show all ({n} characters)** opens the whole, read from its event, as plain text (the web in the browser's own view, the Mac in the file viewer). **Numbers** (before → after; the web's are its work per step in Bun, the Mac's frames in the test renderer; link 80 ms + 4 Mbit/s, gzipped): *open to first paint*: web 23 → 14–18 ms after the frames (≈ 110–175 ms on the link), Mac 57–63 → 60–61 ms, the same at every size. *Scroll from the end to the head*: web each older page 186 ms (2k), 912 ms (10k), 576 ms and rising (50k: never reached the head) → p95 6–7 ms, longest under 50 ms (headless Chrome, 50k: frame p95 18 ms, no long tasks, at most 15 turns in the page); Mac p95 4.6 ms (2k), 570 ms (10k), did not reach the head in 15 min (50k) → 17–18 ms at every size. *Held*: every event loaded (10,000, 50,000, no limit) → at most 2,000 on both. *Jump into the middle*: before, only after loading everything up to it → web 134 ms to the turn on the link (about 50 ms of work over 4 pages), Mac 44 ms (10k), 143 ms (50k). *Live events while scrolled up*: 2.4 ms p95 each, the reader's turns not rebuilt. *Tradeoff:* the Mac at 2,000 events scrolls at 18 ms p95 where it was 4.6 ms, because a turn is now built as it comes into view and hiding keys in its outputs is most of that; a faster redaction is in todo. *Alternative not taken:* keep everything loaded and only virtualize drawing (memory still grows without bound and every page still rebuilt the transcript). | U (the author, 2026-11-17); ## 2026-11-17: one partner, one mailbox, one home answering it; the live trial as its own identity (the author: "bridge 你第一性原理用长期有价值的方式去决定吧"; research/66 §9)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D324 | **Built 2026-11-17 with fakes only (core, protocol, web, Mac, the trial script); nothing was created on the person's Mem; not reviewed by the author; no persona or tool change, so no eval.** *Found:* the live trial stopped because Mem lists two active connections for `ducter`, both labelled `ducter`: hel's Ducter (connected from Settings) and the Mac's own nmem login, connected by hand for the 2026-11-13 trial (the Mac's `~/.ducter` has no `bridge-connection.json`, so no Ducter there reads it; its `ducter` context is the trial's). Whoever reads first takes a message, so one of the person's agents' requests can land where nobody looks, and `connections list` can't say which computer is which. *First principles:* the address is **who** (the partner, D18: one Mem identity, `ducter`, or D312's `ducter-<id>`), the connection is **where** (the home it lives on). A mailbox has exactly one reader, so a partner has exactly one home answering it. A Mem identity per home was rejected: it splits the partner's memory and provenance (D141 binds one identity per partner), and a terminal agent would find two "Ducter"s to choose between; two homes that each want their own address are two partners (D312), each with its own identity. **(1) A connection is owned by one home and named for it.** The context Ducter connects with (Mem shows it as the connection's label) is `<identity>-on-<home>-<key tag>`: the home's name as a slug and six hex of its D293 key fingerprint (two Macs both called "mac" still differ), then `-2`… after a revoked one (Mem never reopens a revoked connection by its old name). `DUCTER_BRIDGE_CONTEXT` still overrides it. A connection made before D324 keeps its name and keeps working; nothing is renamed behind the person's back. **(2) A second home never connects beside the first on its own.** Every look reads Mem's list for the identity (read-only). Another home's active connection: the row is **elsewhere**, **{name} 现在在 {home} 上收你别的 AI 发来的消息，这台不用再收。 / {name} gets your other AI agents' messages on {home} now; this computer doesn't need to.** with one action, **改由这台收 / Receive here instead**, which asks in place (**改由这台收？{home} 上就不再收了…**) and on the Go connects here first, then revokes the other (never a moment with nobody answering). A plain Connect there runs nothing. A client (the Mac app or the phone showing a server home) never has a connection of its own: Bridge belongs to the home's core. **(3) Two readers already (from before D324): one calm row, one action.** Under the connected head: **{name} 也在 {home} 上收 / {name} also receives on {home}** (a label from before D324: **另一台电脑 / another computer**), **两台都在收，你别的 AI 发来的消息会被先查收的那台拿走，可能落到你不看的那边。只留一台就好。**, **只留这台 / Keep only this one**, asking in place (**只留这台？{home} 上的 {name} 就不再收你别的 AI 发来的消息了。**). Mem's revoke is "one own connection": one another login made may be refused from here; then the row says **{home} 上的连接只能在那台上断开：在那台的 Ducter 里打开 设置 › 连上的 AI agent，点「断开」。** and offers nothing it can't do. A home whose connection another home ended notices at its next look or its 30-minute recheck (read-only `connections list`), drops its record, and its checks stop. **(4) Per partner (D312), the same rule:** `ducter-work`'s connection is `ducter-work-on-hel-<tag>`; Bridge per partner is still D312's "Left". **(5) The live trial is its own identity** (`bridge-trial.ts`): `--real` makes `ducter-trial-<yyyymmddhhmm>-<hex>` (a ledger under the evidence folder first; `agents enroll … --source-app ducter-trial`; `connections connect`; a check that Mem lists exactly that one active connection), tells the peer that exact contact, runs S1, S2, S3, X1, and removes all of it (revoke, `agents context clear` with its revision, `agents delete --yes`); a failed removal keeps its ledger for `--cleanup`; only an id of the trial's shape is ever removed. The person's `ducter` is never named. So the trial runs any time, whatever the person has connected, and D258's shared-mailbox guard and `--share-mailbox` are retired. **(6) Upstream, drafts only** (research/66 §9.3, not posted): a host or device label (and `created_at`, `last_seen_at`) on each connection, set at `connect`; whether `revoke` may end a connection of the same member made by another login, and its code when not; `outcome_unknown` as a contract (`false` means not admitted, on every verb, `connect` included); what `agents delete` does to a mailbox and its messages. *Tradeoff:* one more read (`connections list`) per look and every 30 minutes. *Alternative not taken:* a Mem identity per home (`ducter-hel`), which needs no coordination but splits who the partner is. | the author, 2026-11-17; D18, D141, D205, D258, D293, D312 | `design/bridge.md` "One home answers (D324)", "Try it live"; `design/product-model.md` glossary; `design/roadmap.md`; `design/todo.md`; `docs/settings.md`; `research/66` §9; `packages/core/src/{bridge-link,core,ws,main}.ts`; `packages/protocol/src/index.ts`; `packages/partner/eval/{bridge-trial,bridge-live,fake-bridge-nmem}.ts`; `packages/core/test/{bridge-homes,bridge-link}.test.ts`; `packages/partner/test/bridge-trial.test.ts`; `apps/web/src/{memory.tsx,app.ts,i18n-memory.ts}`; `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/protocol.go,views/{peers_pane,app,bridge_test}.go,i18n/memory.go}` |

(1) **The locator lists the session's landmarks**, made from the session index alone (`packages/protocol/src/landmarks.ts`, its Go port, `fixtures/landmarks.json`): each said turn, each report (its first line, now carried by the index's mark with its time, `IndexMark.at`/`w`, cut at 120 with keys hidden), each compaction, switch, move or interruption, and between them each run of quiet turns once; a round that reports is its report. Rows are one height and only those near the list's view are drawn (50,000 events: 1,250 landmarks, about 25 rows drawn, made in under 1 ms). Pointing at the rail chooses the landmark nearest that turn and centers the list on it, those in view marked; a click pins it and gives it the keys (↑↓, Page, Home/End; Return goes there by D284's glide or D320's jump; Esc closes); unpinned it closes 260 ms after the pointer leaves. (2) **Times in order:** an item's time alone today, with its day otherwise; a range always earlier first, both days when it crosses one (**昨天 22:10–今天 1:05**), one time within a minute; never "10:46–10:32" (it was a loop across midnight with no day). *Not taken:* a minimap of the rendered page (its cost grows with the session; it says nothing a fresh user can read). **Part 2, the composer while it works.** *Who:* the developer steering several agents (before: Return steered and nothing ever said whether it was read; 做完再说 handed the words to the agent's own queue, where they could not be changed or taken back, shown as a dashed 排队中 bubble mid-transcript), the consumer (wants to know it was heard), the fresh user (should not need the words steer or queue). *Felt:* 放心 and 顺滑: what Return will do is said before it is pressed, and what happened after. *First time:* type while it works; the placeholder says it. (3) **Idle, Return sends** the next turn. **While it works, Return steers** (placeholder **插一句，它做到下一步就会看到… / Add something; it sees it at its next step…**; hint **回车：它做到下一步就会看到** and **⌥ 回车：这一轮做完再说**; on a phone the placeholder stays **直接跟它说…** and the hint says it). (4) **A steer says when it was read:** the runner keeps it unread until the agent's own echo of it comes (OAR's `user_message`: Claude Code's replay with `--replay-user-messages`, Codex's userMessage item, pi's and DeepSeek Harness's user message; mapped to `user_echo` by the normalizer; matched by its words, and every steer before it counts as read), then logs `raw.read`; under the bubble **它做到下一步就会看到 / It'll see this at its next step** with a working dot while unread, **✓ 它看到了 / Seen** on the newest one read, nothing else. (5) **After this is held by Ducter, not the agent:** the runner holds the person's words (`task_held`, the whole queue on each change; `TaskCard.held`, so every window shows it and a restart keeps it); chips over the composer under **这一轮做完再说 / After this turn**, in order: a click edits one in place (**改好了 / 取消**), **现在就说 / Say it now** steers it in (or starts the turn when idle), **× 不说了 / Take back** drops it (`task_held` frame; one already gone: **这句已经发给它了**). When a turn ends completed, everything held is the next turn, each logged as the person's words in order; after a Stop, a failure, a limit or a compaction it stays held; a send while idle carries it first. The partner's and Ducter's own queued words still use the agent's queue. (6) **An agent that can't steer** (`HarnessInfo.steer`, Go `protocol.NoSteer`): Return holds too, and it says so (**{agent} 做事时不能插话，发出的话会等这一轮做完**, chips' head **{agent} 这一轮做完就会看到**, no 做完再说 or 现在就说 while it works). Per OAR 0.95.1's source, all four steer: Claude Code (stream-json user message written into the running turn), Codex (app-server `turn/steer`), pi (SDK `steer`), DeepSeek Harness (bridge `steer`); OAR's withdraw exists for Claude Code, pi and DeepSeek Harness but not Codex, which is why Ducter holds the queue itself. *Alternative not taken:* OAR's own queue with `withdraw` (no edit or take-back on Codex, and the queue would not survive a restart or show in every window). *Also:* `channels-wechat.test.ts` compared WeChat's reply window to the wall clock instead of the rig's fake clock and failed from today; it reads the rig's clock now; `learned-week.test.ts` steps a week of the fake clock a minute at a time and gets 60 s. | U (the author, 2026-11-17); D207, D268, D271, D284, D315, D320; OAR 0.95.1 source | `packages/protocol/src/{index,internal,harnesses,landmarks,session}.ts`, `packages/protocol/fixtures/{landmarks-cases.ts,landmarks.json,transcript.json}`, `packages/runner/src/{runner,normalize}.ts`, `packages/runner/test/{runner,normalize}.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/{ws,registry}.ts`, `packages/core/test/{idempotent-send,channels-wechat,learned-week}.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/{app,store,views,transcript,format,onhand,i18n-transcript}.ts(x)`, `apps/web/static/{app.css,app.js}`, `apps/web/{demo,demo-steer}.ts`, `apps/web/test/{held,locator-list}.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/{protocol,session}.go,store/store.go,i18n/{turns,loop,when}.go}`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/{held,landmarks,task,taskturns,taskpage,session,app}.go` and their tests, `design/{focus-window,ui,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/getting-started.md` **Held words after a Stop stay held (author, 2026-11-17):** a Stop means "let me think again", so nothing the person held goes out on its own; they go when the person sends again or taps 现在就说. |

## 2026-11-17: a steer's receipt matched by its id, checked live; the locator's name says what it lists (D328; D325's follow-ups)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D328 | **Built 2026-11-17; the echo checked live on Claude Code (haiku), Codex (gpt-6-luna) and pi (MiniMax-M3) through OAR, DeepSeek Harness by OAR's source only (not installed); not reviewed by the author.** *Who:* the developer steering a task (before: the receipt matched the agent's echo by its words, so an echo whose words the agent's side had changed, or two steers alike, could mark the wrong one; after: the same receipt, matched exactly); the screen-reader user on a wide window (before: the locator was named for what was said, but it lists reports and marks too). *Felt:* 放心. (1) **When Seen shows is unchanged**, because live it is already right: each agent echoes at the step its model takes the words in (Claude Code and pi when the tool call they had already chosen ends; Codex at its next sampling, even while a shell runs under its exec cell). A rule holding the echo until running tools end was tried and dropped: on Codex it showed Seen about 8 s late. Seen means read, not obeyed (one Codex run of three read the steer and kept to the brief). (2) **Matched by id:** the runner mints a UUID per steer and passes it as OAR's `inputId` (`HarnessSession.send`'s `inputId`, carried to a worker); the normalizer keeps the echo's `inputId` in `user_echo`; `steerSeen` finds the steer by id, else by its words (pi, which echoes no id; a worker before this change). Claude Code's `uuid` and Codex's `clientId` came back exactly the id passed. (3) **The locator's name** (its rail and card, Mac and web) is **这件事的经过 / What happened in this task** (was **这件事里说过的话 / What was said in this task**): literal, and true of what D325 made it list. *Alternative not taken:* **跳到这件事里的某一处 / Jump to a point in this task** (names the act, but a list read aloud should say what it holds). | D325, research/116 | `packages/protocol/src/internal.ts`, `packages/runner/src/{runner,normalize,oar,remote,worker-host}.ts`, `packages/runner/test/{runner,normalize}.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/i18n-transcript.ts`, `apps/web/static/app.js`, `apps/desktop/internal/i18n/loop.go`, `design/{focus-window,product-model,todo}.md`, `research/{116-steer-live,README}.md` |

## 2026-11-17: Use this phone with Ducter closed or the phone locked (D331; the author, on 0.0.66 with a real Pixel Fold: "不解锁，不打开 app 就没法用")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D331 | **Built 2026-11-17 on the Android app, the home, the protocol, the web and the Mac; checked with Android unit tests, the home's socket tests with a bridge-4 fake phone (`handset-d331.test.ts`), web and Mac word tests; not yet on a real phone (the steps are in `todo.md`), not reviewed by the author.** *Who:* the consumer who taps 借给它 on their Mac while the Pixel is in their pocket (before: nothing happened until they opened Ducter on the phone, an hour on hel, and the task said a card was still asking; after: the loan starts with Ducter closed, or the phone says on its lock screen that it starts when they unlock); the developer locking the phone mid-test (before: the lock gave it back and a new card asked; after: the loan pauses and the phone asks once, after the unlock); the fresh user (nothing new to learn: Go, then their phone tells them the one thing to do). *Feel:* 顺滑 (Go is enough), 放心 (never through the lock; never resumes by itself; the lock screen shows no task title), 好用 (one tap on the phone, no new card). Evidence: research/119; the Log of task vrxcdgr9. **(1) The phone's own link holds while Android's switch for Ducter is on, lent or not** (bridge 4, `HandsetLinkService`): started by the accessibility service when it connects, by the page's hello, on screen-on and unlock, and by a loan; its token is the page's or the copy the app keeps for the device (D293); not lent its notification is a quiet **用这台手机开着 / Use this phone is on** on its own channel (the person may hide it); retries back off to a minute when not lent, and the screen coming on or the unlock retries at once; a home that refuses the device (401/403) stops it. The home prefers it (D255) and still takes the page's. It reaches the phone at once while the screen is on or the phone is picked up; in deep Doze only as far as Android lets a foreground service's socket through (research/119 §3; Battery › Unrestricted makes it sure). No FCM: a self-hosted home has no other wake path (research/119 §3). **(2) A Go on a locked phone never goes through the lock.** The phone holds it as waiting (`waiting`) and shows **解锁后，「{task}」就开始 / "{task}" starts when you unlock** (on the lock screen only **解锁后，Ducter 就开始用这台手机**), with **不借了 / Not now**; on unlock (`ACTION_USER_PRESENT`) it says so to the home, which starts the loan: nobody opens Ducter. The home keeps the states apart and says each truthfully, in the tool's words, the opened task (web and Mac) and the resolved card (**借给它了，还没开始**): the card asking (**Waiting for the user to answer the card…**); Go given, the phone locked (**借给它了：解锁你的 {phone} 就开始**); Go given, the phone out of reach (**借给它了：现在连不上你的 {phone}，连上就开始**) with why as far as known: Android limits Ducter in the background (Battery › Unrestricted), its Ducter too old to hold its own link, offline or closed, never heard since the home started; Go given, starting; lent. Fixes the tool text that said "a card is asking them" after a Go. **(3) Locking during a loan pauses it** (supersedes D253's "locking gives it back"): the pill goes, the screen may sleep, nothing runs, the loan's notification says **「{task}」暂停了** with Stop still there; the task hears it once and its tools say the phone is locked and to end the turn; no quiet or lost rule while paused (a locked phone may not answer). On unlock the task does not take control: a notification asks **还借给「{task}」吗？** with **继续借给它 / Keep lending** and **不借了 / Not now** (one tap on the phone, no new card); Keep lending carries on where it was (**{phone} answers again and is still lent to you…**), Not now ends it as the person's (`taken`; the next tool asks with one new card). Stop still gives it back at once. **The cap: a pause ends the loan after 30 minutes** (`expired`, both sides), or when the task ends. Why 30: the yes was for "a while" (用一会儿); short pauses (a test's lock, a glance at a message, a coffee) are minutes; past half an hour the person has moved on and an old yes coming back is a surprise, while a new card costs one tap; the notification after the unlock never resumes by itself anyway, so the cap only bounds how long a task waits on a phone in a pocket. Alternatives: lock gives it back (D253; the author's tests showed it breaks every lock-and-check step); resume by itself on unlock (the person may be using their phone; rejected); no cap (a forgotten loan holding a task for hours). An app before bridge 4 keeps D253's behaviour. | U (the author, 2026-11-17), research/119, D238, D253, D255, D280, D293 | `research/119-phone-link-background.md`; `design/{use-this-phone,product-model,scenarios,todo}.md`, `docs/phone.md`, `packages/runner/src/brief.ts`; `apps/android/app/src/main/java/co/nowledge/ducter/android/{Handset,HandsetLife,HandsetLink,HandsetPill,Notify,MainActivity}.kt`, `apps/android/app/src/main/{AndroidManifest.xml,res/values/strings.xml,res/values-zh/strings.xml}`, tests `apps/android/app/src/test/java/co/nowledge/ducter/android/{HandsetLifeTest,HandsetLinkTest}.kt`; `packages/protocol/src/{handset,index}.ts`, `packages/core/src/{handset/index,ws,core}.ts`, tests `packages/core/test/{handset-d331,handset-life}.test.ts`; `apps/web/src/{handset.tsx,i18n-handset.ts}`, `apps/web/test/handset-d331.test.ts`; `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/{handset,protocol}.go,store/phoneuse.go,i18n/handset.go,views/handset.go}`, `apps/desktop/internal/views/handset_d331_test.go` |

## 2026-11-17: Nowledge Mem, deeper: one line in the first words, a save that replaces instead of piling up, Undo, a save that waits while Mem is away, Mem's closed app, Mem in Update all (D329; the brief: "make the Nowledge Mem integration feel deep and lovely")

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D329 | **Built 2026-11-17 on the home, the partner, the protocol, the web and the Mac, checked with a stub nmem, fake Mem clients, fake installers, unit and view tests and shots (`.shots/d329/web`, `.shots/d329/mac`, zh and en, light and dark); not yet against a real Mem (the outbox's upsert key, `m supersede`, `m archive` and `m show` are Mem's documented commands, unchecked live).** *Who:* the Mem user (Cloud or the local app) whose Claude Code and Codex already write to the same Mem; the heavy developer who says the same preference twice in a month and sees two lines; the fresh user who never heard of Mem and only ever sees one quiet line. *Feel:* before, Mem was a store Ducter wrote into: the same preference saved twice was two memories, a wrong save could only be forgotten (it asks), a save while Mem was down was dropped without a word, a closed Mem app read as "not signed in", and Mem's update was its own errand outside 全部更新; after, a save that restates or changes something the partner already remembered takes its place, a wrong one is undone in one tap, a save while Mem is away waits and goes in by itself, the closed app is one line and one tap, and one tap updates everything. *First time:* nothing to learn: the Noted line in a reply's Details says what happened, in words. **(1) The first words say Mem is there, and read nothing of it** (D298's `memLine` hook, wired; D327's rule holds for every source). With memory on and the home's Mem answering signed in at the start's look (`nmem status`, read-only), one line after the greeting: **你的 Nowledge Mem 我也接上了：你跟别的 AI 交代过的习惯，用得着的时候我会想起来。/ I'm on your Nowledge Mem too: whatever you told your other AI tools about how you like things, I'll recall when it matters.**, and one start **你都记得我些什么？/ What do you remember about me?** whose tap fills the composer; sent, the partner recalls then, because it was asked. Mem is a source the person chose to share across tools, but quoting a memory at the first second is still an unprompted read on a screen that may be shared (research/115: unprompted reading was the creepiest variant). Alternatives: a line quoting what Mem holds (D298's plan; rejected for that reason), nothing (the Mem user's 惊喜 lost; they should know at once that their other tools' memory is here). **(2) Search before writing, supersede instead of duplicating.** `memory_add` asks Mem for its title (beside the write, so a save takes no longer) and, when a hit is the partner's own earlier memory (Mem `source` `ducter`, its words whole, never clipped) whose title is alike (character pairs, script-agnostic: Dice ≥ 0.6, or one title holding the other at ≥ 4 characters), links it to the new one (`nmem m supersede <old> <new>`). Another tool's memories and the person's own are never replaced from here. The Noted line says **换掉了之前那条「{title}」/ In place of “{title}”** as its own element; the partner's words never mention it. A title rule catches a restatement and the same topic said anew ("Weekly report day"); a changed preference titled differently is still a second memory (a semantic judge by the model is in `todo.md`). **(3) 撤销 / Undo on a fresh Noted line.** While the person hasn't said anything since, the line offers **撤销 / Undo**, no question asked (it is the undo): the memory is archived in Mem (`nmem m archive`: out of everyday recall, kept audit-readable; never deleted), a memory it replaced is written back from its own words (`m show`, then a plain save; Mem has no un-supersede), and a save still waiting in the outbox is dropped before it reaches Mem. The line then reads **不记了「{title}」/ Not kept “{title}”** (`MemView.undone`). When Mem doesn't answer, the line stays and says **Nowledge Mem 没回应，还记着 / Nowledge Mem didn't answer; still noted**. After the person's next message the line offers **忘掉 / Forget** as before (D304: asks, reaches Mem). Alternatives: Undo always (a week-old line's "undo" is a forget and should ask), confirm before Undo (an undo that asks is not an undo). **(4) A save while Mem is away waits** (research/private/10 §"Mem down ≠ Ducter down"). When Mem is installed and signed in but doesn't answer (`unavailable`, not `not_configured`: nothing waits for a Mem that isn't there), the save goes to an outbox (`<partner dir>/mem-outbox.json`, 0600) under a key made from what it is (persona, Log seq, task, words; UUID-shaped), and the partner treats it as remembered. It goes in on the next Mem call that works and every 5 minutes, naming the key as Mem's own upsert id (`nmem m add --id`), so a save Mem took on a try that seemed to fail is still one memory; a key Mem refuses is tried once more without it; a save that waited 30 days is let go (memories are an index of the Log, never its only copy). The line says **等 Nowledge Mem 回来就存进去 / Goes into Nowledge Mem once it's back** until it does (`MemView.waiting`). The first try of a save still names no id: the key's shape is unchecked against a live Mem. **(5) Mem's app closed: one line and a way to open it** (the trigger "Mem exposes how to start it" is met by macOS's own `open`). A failed `nmem status` that is a refused connection to this computer (loopback) is `mem_closed`, no longer read as "not signed in": **Nowledge Mem 没开着 / Nowledge Mem isn't open**; on a Mac home with the app, **{home} 上的 Nowledge Mem 应用关着，记忆先放着，打开就接上。** with **打开 Nowledge Mem / Open Nowledge Mem** (`bridge_mem_open`: the home runs `open -a` on the person's tap, then looks again for up to 20 s); elsewhere **在 {home} 上打开 Nowledge Mem 应用就好。/ Open the Nowledge Mem app on {home}.** A remote Mem server that is down is not "closed". **(6) Nowledge Mem in 全部更新 / Update all** (D257 option C). The home's `nmem`, when Mem says a newer one is out and Ducter can update this copy from its own source (D229; never the app's copy), is one item, **{device} 上的 Nowledge Mem / Nowledge Mem on {device}** (`kind: "mem"`, `mem:local`), always shown on the card (never under 还有 N 项), and the order note names it (**…最后是 {home} 上的 Nowledge Mem。**); after the agents, once the home's own Ducter step is over (its restart would cut the update off); by day only (the night takes only versions Ducter checked). A home that restarted mid-way judges it by what Mem says then. **(7) Memory shows Mem's own memories, by kind** (D257, research/84 §4): closed by D321, which built it (the groups by Mem's kind, each line's source, Fix and Forget in Mem); what was left, reading the identity's lane in the glance as recall does, is its own line in `todo.md`. Persona and partner tool names and descriptions unchanged (no D175 eval); only `memory_add`'s result note names a replaced memory. | U (the brief of 2026-11-17), D257, D298, D304, D321, D327, research/115, research/private/10 | `design/{memory,product-model,scenarios,todo,onboarding}.md`, `docs/{settings,faq,install,devices}.md`; `packages/partner/src/{memory,outbox,partner}.ts`, `packages/core/src/{bridge-link,update-all,first-words,settings,ws,core,main}.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/{index,internal}.ts`, tests `packages/partner/test/{memory,memory-d329}.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/mem-d329.test.ts`; `apps/web/src/{views.tsx,memory.tsx,mem-view.ts,updateall.tsx,app.ts,store.ts,i18n.ts,i18n-memory.ts,i18n-updateall.ts}`, `apps/web/static/app.css`, `apps/web/{demo-noted,demo-memory,demo-updateall}.ts`, test `apps/web/test/d329.test.ts`; `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/protocol.go,store/store.go,i18n/{memd329,memory,updateall}.go,mock/updateall.go,views/{quiet,memory,memory_pane,peers,peers_pane,updateall}.go}`, tests `apps/desktop/internal/{protocol/memd329_test.go,views/{d329,d329_updateall,memory}_test.go}` |

## 2026-11-17: the home reads its Bridge mailbox every minute, soon after it writes, and long-polls once Mem can hold a read (D335)

| # | Decision | Source | Reflected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| D335 | **Built 2026-11-17 with fakes only (a fake clock for the timers, the fake nmem's `inbox --wait`); not reviewed by the author; no persona or partner-tool change, so no eval.** *Who:* the heavy developer whose terminal agent asks the partner something and waits, or who asked the partner to ask one; the consumer and the fresh user never see it (nothing new to read or set). *Feel:* before, an answer sat in the mailbox up to 5 min (a minute while live), so a back-and-forth felt like email; after, an answer to what the partner just sent is read within seconds, and anything else within a minute. *Why it is cheap:* Mem's `bridge inbox` is pull-only (a long-poll, `inbox --wait`, is asked for upstream on nowledge-co/mem#10402); one read is a short local CLI call, one at a time, and nothing wakes the partner unless a new message is there. **(1) The period is 1 min** (was 5 min). **(2) After the partner sends or replies** (`bridge_reply`, a send the person tapped on a card, the claim and result Ducter sends by code): reads at +10 s, 30 s, 1 min and 2 min after it; the rest are cancelled once the answer to that message arrives (`in_reply_to`). **(3) While live** with one of the person's own agents (D164 (6): 30 min after a message from or to one), every 15 s (was 60 s). **(4) The long-poll when the CLI has it:** `nmem bridge inbox --help` is read once per nmem version (D205's way); when it lists `--wait`, one `inbox --wait 25` at a time, back to back, per context, replaces the timer for arrivals (a handle new to the Log runs the usual check; a wait that comes back at once with nothing new pauses 15 s), and the timer drops to every 5 min for recovery and follow-through only. A wait that errors hands arrivals back to the timer (1 min), which tries the long-poll again after 10 min. `bridgeIntervalMs: 0` still means "at start and when asked" only. **With D334's Spaces** the long-poll runs per Space context (one loop per place; when wide, one `inbox --all-spaces --wait` on the home's context, if the help lists both); a handle from any place runs the one check, which reads every place; a place whose wait errors goes back to the timer alone (the timer stays at 1 min until every place waits again), and only that place is retried after 10 min; a new client (places or context changed) starts its own loops. *Tradeoff:* about 60 reads an hour per home instead of 12, each a local process start and one Mem request. *Alternative:* keep 5 min and only the reads after a send (cheaper, but a message from an agent that wasn't answering one of ours still waits up to 5 min). | the author's brief, 2026-11-17; D164 (6), D205, D333; nowledge-co/mem#10402 | `design/{bridge,todo}.md`; `packages/partner/src/{partner,bridge,bridge-out}.ts`, `packages/partner/eval/fake-bridge-nmem.ts`, `packages/partner/test/bridge-cadence.test.ts` |
